repairs.rule: undeclared optional inverse is reduced to null

design_principles: Types generalize across domains; episode-specific wording is never encoded.
Predicates are operational: each is usable for graph reads/writes with typed endpoints.
All inverses are declared within this schema or null.
Upper types describe broad participation semantics; biological species, materials, and weather kinds are concepts linked through classified_as.

entity_types.name: person
entity_types.definition: A human individual, including the operator and other people; no operator-specific type exists in the core schema.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Any human mentioned as an actor, owner, or relation endpoint.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Non-human actors (see agent) and groups of people (see organization).

entity_types.name: agent
entity_types.definition: An autonomous or semi-autonomous software actor (assistant, persona, AI agent) that can perform actions, hold goals, or exchange messages.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Named AI assistants, agent personas, harnesses acting as agents.

entity_types.name: organization
entity_types.definition: A collective human entity such as a company, team, or institution.

entity_types.name: organism
entity_types.definition: A living entity other than a person when specialized human handling is not appropriate, including animals, plants, fungi, and unknown living things.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Named or individuated non-human living entities; biological kinds remain concept classifications rather than upper types.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Humans (person); non-living material things (object); software actors (agent).

entity_types.name: object
entity_types.definition: A discrete tangible material thing, natural or manufactured, represented primarily by its physical identity.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Physical items such as rocks, furniture, devices, vehicles, and manufactured instances.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Living things (person, organism); locations (place); occurrences (event, phenomenon); authored informational or design works (artifact).

entity_types.name: place
entity_types.definition: A physical, geographic, or administratively bounded location in which entities may be located or occurrences may happen.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Rooms, buildings, campsites, cities, regions, countries, and named geographic features treated as locations.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Organizations associated with a location; physical objects merely occupying a location; events occurring there.

entity_types.name: artifact
entity_types.definition: A created informational, expressive, or functional work—such as a document, paper, media work, repository, protocol specification, software tool, or design deliverable—represented primarily by its authored or designed identity.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Created works that are authored, hosted, shared, reviewed, or versioned, rather than individual tangible instances.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Discrete tangible instances (object); running software systems (system); projects (project); abstract notions (concept).

entity_types.name: system
entity_types.definition: A running or deployable software/hardware system, harness, platform, or infrastructure component that hosts or executes other software.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Harnesses, pipelines, platforms, deployed software systems.

entity_types.name: project
entity_types.definition: A time-bounded effort with goals and deliverables, possibly spanning systems and artifacts.

entity_types.name: concept
entity_types.definition: An abstract idea, topic, design concept, method, risk, or problem class referenced in reasoning or discussion.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Design ideas, mechanisms, risks, technical problems, topics.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Concrete created objects (artifact) or medical states (condition).

entity_types.name: condition
entity_types.definition: A medical or health-related state, trait, or deficiency attributable to a person or organism.

entity_types.name: event
entity_types.definition: A temporally located occurrence, conversation, trip, or milestone that can be ordered in time.

entity_types.name: phenomenon
entity_types.definition: An observable process, state, or pattern unfolding in the world that is not best represented as a discrete event or persistent object.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Weather and natural appearances or processes such as rain, cloud cover, smoke, and rainbows when treated as observed phenomena.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Discrete temporally bounded occurrences (event); material things (object); abstract explanatory ideas (concept).

entity_types.name: gap
entity_types.definition: A known deficiency in capability, retrieval, or knowledge that the system or operator has identified and may address.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Retrieval gaps, demonstrated failure modes, known unknowns.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Abstract problem topics without an identified deficiency instance (concept).

entity_types.name: other_thing
entity_types.definition: A governed fallback for an entity that cannot yet be represented by any declared upper type without semantic distortion.
entity_types.inclusion_rule: Use only after all declared types are considered; preserve the original descriptor and flag repeated use for ontology-extension review.
entity_types.exclusion_rule: Anything that can reasonably use a declared upper type; never use merely because the domain-specific classification is absent.

predicates.name: part_of
predicates.definition: Subject is a constituent component or member of the object.

predicates.name: has_part
predicates.definition: Subject contains the object as a constituent component or member.

predicates.name: works_at
predicates.definition: Subject is currently affiliated with or employed by the object organization.

predicates.name: formerly_at
predicates.definition: Subject was previously affiliated with or employed by the object organization.

predicates.name: operates
predicates.definition: Subject person or agent uses and controls the object agent or system as its operator.

predicates.name: owns
predicates.definition: Subject has ownership or lasting custodianship of the object.

predicates.name: authored
predicates.definition: Subject person, agent, or organization created the object artifact or system.

predicates.name: leads
predicates.definition: Subject has leadership or decision authority over the object project.

predicates.name: works_on
predicates.definition: Subject is actively contributing effort to the object project or artifact.

predicates.name: addresses
predicates.definition: Subject artifact or concept is intended to resolve or mitigate the object gap or concept-problem.

predicates.name: affects
predicates.definition: Subject condition, concept, or phenomenon has an impact on the object person, organism, object, place, system, condition, or concept.

predicates.name: has_condition
predicates.definition: Subject person or organism has the object medical condition or trait.

predicates.name: uses
predicates.definition: Subject person or agent employs the object artifact, system, or protocol in their activity.

predicates.name: considered_using
predicates.definition: Subject person or agent has evaluated but not necessarily adopted the object artifact, system, or protocol.

predicates.name: implements
predicates.definition: Subject artifact or system realizes the object concept, protocol, or design in concrete form.

predicates.name: occurs_after
predicates.definition: Subject event happens temporally after the object event.

predicates.name: related_to
predicates.definition: Generic associative link between any two entities when no more specific predicate applies.

predicates.name: proposed
predicates.definition: Subject agent or person put forward the object concept, artifact, project, or system as an idea or plan.

predicates.name: recommends
predicates.definition: Subject person or agent advises adopting or following the object artifact, protocol, concept, or system.

predicates.name: warned_about
predicates.definition: Subject person or agent cautioned about the risk or drawback described by the object concept.

predicates.name: keeps_secret_from
predicates.definition: Subject person or agent deliberately withholds information from the object agent or person.

predicates.name: runs_on
predicates.definition: Subject agent, system, or artifact executes within or depends on the object system or artifact as its runtime environment.

predicates.name: managed_with
predicates.definition: Subject condition is managed or mitigated using the object artifact, system, or concept.

predicates.name: has_gap
predicates.definition: Subject person, agent, system, or project currently exhibits the object unresolved gap.

predicates.name: plans_migration_of
predicates.definition: Subject person, agent, or organization intends or plans migration of the object agent or system.

predicates.name: migrates_to
predicates.definition: Subject agent or system is intended to migrate to the object destination system.

predicates.name: classified_as
predicates.definition: Subject is categorized by the object concept; this domain classification does not change the subject's upper ontology type.

predicates.name: located_at
predicates.definition: Subject is physically located in, associated with, or occurs at the object place for the evidenced time or scope.

extension_policy.proposal_threshold: An extension is admitted only when a recurring relation cannot be expressed by a core predicate without semantic distortion; extensions are first-class predicates with full type declarations.
extension_policy.required_evidence: At least two distinct future episodes or a structural necessity in the graph read path.
extension_policy.consolidation_rule: When an extension's usage stabilizes, it may be promoted to core; when unused across a consolidation window, it is dropped.

risks: related_to may become a catch-all; usage should be monitored and promoted to specific predicates when patterns emerge.
protocol as artifact conflates specification and standard; if protocols become first-class actors in coordination episodes, consider a distinct protocol type.
gap vs concept boundary depends on whether a deficiency is instantiated as an addressable node; ambiguous cases should default to concept until actionable.

curation.rationale: The graph traverses asserted edges in either direction; unused inverse labels duplicate vocabulary.
Real baseline facts otherwise mapped with semantic distortion or incompatible signatures.
Observed person-to-agent operation and person-to-system authorship are valid domain cases.
Declared core relations and evidence-specific meanings replace false extensions and distorted mappings.

curation.rule: generalize world entities without creating a domain taxonomy
curation.rationale: Living kinds such as plant, dog, and cat are classifications, not upper types. Tangible things, locations, and observable phenomena need distinct participation semantics. other_thing is a governed fallback whose recurrence signals that the ontology should be extended.
